discouraging imports. This may help to increase the country’s exports and
decrease imports, and may therefore help to reduce the current account deficit.

options.label: A

options.option_text:
To act as independent regulator in case
of applications for loans of Rs. 50 crore or more

options.label: D
options.option_text:
To aim at faster resolution of stressed
assets of Rs. 50 crore or more which are under consortium lending

questions.solution_text:
Inter-Creditor Agreement (ICA)
Option  d)  is  correct:  Inter-Creditor
Agreement (ICA) aimed at faster resolution of stressed assets of Rs. 50 crore
or more which are under consortium lending. It has been signed by 22 public
sector banks, 19 private sector banks and 32 foreign banks and 12 major
financial intermediaries like LIC, HUDCO
etc. ICA Framework is part of project ‘Sashak’. Under it, lead lender (having
highest exposure) will be authorised to formulate resolution plan for operation
turnaround of assets which will be presented to lenders for their approval. It
will be applicable to all corporate borrowers who have availed loans and
financial assistance for amount of Rs. 50 crore or more under consortium
lending or multiple banking arrangements. Each resolution plan will be
submitted by lead lender to Overseeing Committee. The decision making under ICA
framework will be by way of approval of majority lenders i.e. lenders with 66%
share in aggregate exposure. Once resolution plan is approved by majority
lenders, it will be binding on all lenders that are party to ICA. The plan
formulated under ICA will be in compliance with RBI norms and all other
applicable laws and guidelines. Banks opposing resolution plan will have option
to sell their stressed loans to company at discount or buy out loans to that
entity from all other lenders at premium.

questions.solution_text:
Opportunity cost is what a business owner misses out on when selecting one option over another. Opportunity cost represents the benefits an individual, investor, or business misses out on when choosing one alternative over another.
If a commodity is provided free to the public by the Government, then the opportunity cost is transferred from the consumers of the product to the tax-paying public.
As per microeconomics, the opportunity cost is zero for free goods such as air and common goods such as fish/grazing land.

Why does the Government of India promote
the use of 'Neem-coated Urea' in agriculture?

options.label: A
options.option_text:
Release of Neem oil in the soil increases
nitrogen fixation by the soil microorganisms

options.label: B
options.option_text:
Neem coating slows down the rate of
dissolution of urea in the soil

options.label: C
options.option_text:
Nitrous oxide, which is a greenhouse gas,
is not at all released into atmosphere by crop fields

options.label: D
options.option_text:
It is a combination of a weedicide and a
fertilizer for particular crops

questions.solution_text:
When ordinary urea is applied, it gets
converted to ammonium carbamate. Some of this gets converted to ammonia gas in
what is called ammonia volatilisation. The rest of the ammonium carbamate
undergoes chemical transfor-mation and nitrates are formed. Some of these are
absorbed by the plants. The rest are either leached into the underground water
or are denitrified to gaseous nitrogen and nitrous oxide under anaerobic
conditions (absence of oxygen). Neem has properties that check nitrogen loss at
each stage. It slows down the process of nitrate formation and hence excess
nitrate is not available for denitrification.

Consider the following statements in respect of the digital
rupee:
It is a
     sovereign currency issued by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) in alignment
     with its monetary policy.
It appears as
     a liability on the RBI’s balance sheet.
It is insured
     against inflation by its very design.
It is freely
     convertible against commercial bank money and cash.
Which of the statements given above are correct ?
questions.solution_text:
Statement 1
is correct. The digital rupee, or Central
Bank Digital Currency (CBDC), is indeed a sovereign currency issued by the
Reserve Bank of India. It is designed to complement the existing forms of money
and is aligned with the RBI's broader monetary policy objectives.
Statement 2
is also correct. Similar to physical
currency, the digital rupee would appear as a liability on the balance sheet of
the RBI. This is because it represents a claim against the central bank by the
holder of the digital currency.
Statement 3 incorrect.
The digital rupee, like any
currency, is not inherently insured against inflation. Its value would be
subject to the same economic forces that affect the value of physical currency,
including inflationary pressures. The statement that it is insured against
inflation by design is not accurate as no currency can inherently protect
against the loss of purchasing power due to inflation.
Statement 4
is correct. The digital rupee is intended
to be freely convertible against other forms of money, including commercial
bank deposits and cash. This convertibility is crucial for its functionality as
a medium of exchange, allowing users to seamlessly transact and convert between
digital and traditional forms of money.

hydroprocessing
.

reducing emissions by allowing entities to buy and sell carbon credits. This

and has been adopted by many countries and regions as a strategy to mitigate

markets, companies or entities that emit fewer greenhouse gases than their
allotted limit can sell their excess credits to those who exceed their limit.
This allows for a more efficient allocation of emission reduction efforts.
While carbon markets involve financial transactions and can transfer resources
from the private sector to the state. Instead, they facilitate the exchange of
emission allowances between entities, which can include both private and public
entities.
But statement II is not the correct explanation of Statement I:
As it
transfers resources from the private sector to the State it does not become the
reason why they are likely to be one of the most widespread tools in the fight
against climate change.

over the base year. So,
statement 2 is correct.
